title: Pregnancy-related neural and hormonal changes associated with depression risk – PlasMa
summary: This study examines the extent to which pregnancy-related neural plasticity, hormonal changes, and the risk of postnatal depression are linked. The aim is to recruit 400 women who have never been pregnant and are planning to become pregnant in the near future, in order to accompany them throughout their pregnancy. To investigate our research question, we will perform magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before and after pregnancy. We will also record hormonal changes and the course of depressive symptoms throughout the entire pregnancy.
conditions: No specific illness or health issue is being investigated.

interventions.name: As part of this retrospective observational study, women who have never been pregnant and are planning to become pregnant within the next year will be included to determine the relationship between pregnancy-related neural plasticity, hormonal changes, and the risk of postnatal depression. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
a) >=18 years
b) sufficient proficiency in German
c) planning to become pregnant within the next year
d) existing health insurance
e) ability to provide consent
Exclusion criteria:
a) current depressive episode
b) previous pregnancy (including elective and spontaneous abortions)
c) Long-term medication that significantly disrupts the production and function of reproductive hormones
d) Current medication with antidepressants
e) MRI incompatibility
f) Known diagnoses that significantly impacts fertility

Note: Reproductive medical treatment that was started after the baseline measurement does not lead to exclusion from the study.
